title: View of Bangkok (coloured aquatint)
artist: John Heaviside Clark (engraver), after a drawing signed 'H.A.C.'; published by Henry Colburn, London, 1828 (plate from John Crawfurd, 'Journal of an Embassy to the Courts of Siam and Cochin-China')
collection: Wikimedia Commons (British / library scan of the 1828 hand-coloured aquatint)
border: Printed plate with a caption strip in the lower margin ('Drawn by H.A.C.', 'Pub. by H. Colburn London 1828', 'J. Clark sculp'). The image itself is clean; trim the lower caption margin (and thin plate margins) before use.
fit: Strong colour veduta of the ACTUAL city: the Chao Phraya (Menam) river at Bangkok with a Chinese junk in the foreground, riverside stilt houses, and the gilded prang/spires of the royal temples on the skyline. Genuine period colour, correct place, good landscape aspect ratio. The best colour Bangkok illustration found.

_note: Other Bangkok colour leads were checked and rejected: 'View of the city of Bangkok 1822' (Crawfurd) and the two Le Tour du Monde plates ('Vue de la pagode royale', 'Entree du palais du roi de Siam') all turned out to be MONOCHROME engravings; the large c.1879-1881 'Temple of the Emerald Buddha' Commons file is a monochrome PHOTOGRAPH (barred by the illustration rule). So Bangkok yields one solid colour candidate (above). Further colour Bangkok plates likely exist in the David Rumsey collection / Bowring 1857, but were not retrievable here (Wikimedia rate-limiting) and are not on Commons as standalone colour files.
